title: 11-Day Mysuru Dasara Begins With Traditional Inauguration at Chamundi Hills
excerpt: Karnataka's state festival runs October 11-21, culminating in the golden-howdah Jamboo Savari procession on Vijayadashami.
body:
• Karnataka's state festival, Mysuru Dasara, opened on October 11 with the traditional inauguration atop Chamundi Hills, beginning 11 days of ceremonies, cultural events and the famous illuminated palace.
  • The celebrations culminate on October 21 with the Jamboo Savari — the golden-howdah elephant procession carrying Goddess Chamundeshwari — during the auspicious Meena Lagna, 4:10 to 4:35 pm.
  • Chief Minister D K Shivakumar is presiding over the festivities, which include a flower show, food mela, wrestling, Kambala, cultural evenings and a 90-day Dasara expo.
  • For diaspora visitors: Mysuru Palace illumination is the must-see; book travel and accommodation now as the city fills up for Vijayadashami week, and check traffic diversions along the Jamboo Savari route.

Nada Habba begins

Mysuru's 11-day Dasara — Karnataka's Nada Habba, or state festival — began on Sunday with the traditional inauguration at Chamundi Hills, the hill shrine of Goddess Chamundeshwari whose victory over the demon Mahishasura the festival celebrates. Abhinava Gavisiddeshwara Mahaswamy, seer of the Gavi mutt of Koppal, offered puja to the idol of the goddess between 11:50 am and 12:13 pm during the auspicious Dhanur Lagna, alongside Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara.

""We wanted to preserve the heritage, values and culture of Dasara."

The festival's royal form was shaped over centuries by the Wadiyar dynasty, and the modern celebration keeps the two faces of Dasara intact: the religious ceremonies at the palace and Chamundi Hills, and the public cultural program that draws lakhs of visitors from across India and abroad every year.

The 11-day schedule

The government's official calendar runs October 11 to October 21, with the biggest rituals packed into the final stretch. On October 18, Mahanavami and Durgashtami rituals take place at the Mysuru Palace, and the Chief Minister launches a two-day Kambala — the traditional buffalo race — at Saathgalli. October 19 is Ayudha Puja. On Vijayadashami, October 21, the day begins with the Nandi Dhwaja Puja at the palace's Balarama gate (1:36 to 1:56 pm, Makara Lagna), followed by the floral benediction to the golden howdah carrying Goddess Chamundeshwari (4:10 to 4:35 pm, Meena Lagna) that launches the Jamboo Savari. Governor Tawar Chand Gehlot will attend the torchlight parade at Bannimantap ground at 7 pm.

Beyond the procession

The festival's cultural program is as dense as its rituals. The Chief Minister will launch Dasara cultural evenings in front of the illuminated Mysuru Palace and present the state-level Sangeetha Vidwan award to Mysuru Nagamani Srinath. An 11-day flower show runs at Kuppanna Park and Lingambudi lake (9 am to 9 pm), a 15-day food mela at Maharaja's College ground (11 am to 10 pm), four days of wrestling at the D Devaraj Urs stadium, a state-level CM Cup sports meet, and a 90-day Dasara expo. The government is also considering inviting internationally renowned singers — though officials stress Karnataka's culture and traditions remain the central focus.

"We wanted to preserve the heritage, values and culture of Dasara. It is an international festival, and we will continue to make it better and conduct it in a more disciplined manner," the Chief Minister said at the schedule announcement, adding that measures against the misuse of Dasara passes are also on the agenda.

Diaspora angle

For NRIs planning a festive-season trip home, the timing is excellent: Dasara week is when Mysuru shows its best face — the palace outlined in thousands of lights after sunset, markets at their busiest, and the full cultural program running. Arrive well before October 21 if the Jamboo Savari is the goal; streets around the palace-to-Bannimantap route close and fill early, and viewing arrangements and ticketed seating change year to year. Full dates and event guidance are available in the Mysuru Dasara 2026 guide.

What's next

The festival now runs its course through October 21. Watch the Jamboo Savari and the torchlight parade as the set pieces, and the government's visitor-experience measures — pass discipline, crowd management along the procession route — as the operational test of this year's edition. Schedule coverage is also available via New Kerala and 10BM News.
